vocabulary.meaning_en: before now; in the past (after a time period)
vocabulary.note_ar: يأتي بعد المدة: three days ago
vocabulary.note_en: Comes after the period: three days ago.
vocabulary.example: I got this paper three days ago.

vocabulary.meaning_en: after now; in the future (after a time period)
vocabulary.example: Two days from now, it will be Tuesday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: after a period of time from now (future)
vocabulary.example: In three days, it will be Tuesday.

vocabulary.note_ar: نقول a week ago وليس seven days ago
vocabulary.note_en: We say "a week ago", not "seven days ago".
vocabulary.example: A week ago, I started my new job.
We need to talk about time accurately.
For the future, count forward: Monday, Tuesday...
For the past, count backwards: Saturday, Friday...

vocabulary.meaning_en: the second working day of the week
vocabulary.note_ar: Tues تشبه صوت two (الثاني) للتمييز عن Thursday
vocabulary.note_en: "Tues" sounds like "two" – it helps you not confuse it with Thursday.
vocabulary.example: If today is Sunday, two days from now will be Tuesday.

fine_lines.title: ago vs before
fine_lines.explanation_ar: للحديث عن وقت في الماضي محسوبًا من الآن نقول ago: two months ago. لا نقول two months before بهذا المعنى (خطأ شائع).
fine_lines.explanation_en: To talk about a past time counted from now, say "ago": two months ago. Don't say "two months before" for this (a common mistake).

examples.sentence: I was there two months ago.
✗ I was there two months before.

fine_lines.title: ago vs from now / in
fine_lines.explanation_ar: ago للماضي مع was. from now و in للمستقبل مع will be. in تأتي في أول العبارة: in three days.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Ago" for the past with "was". "From now" and "in" for the future with "will be". "In" comes first: in three days.

examples.sentence: Three days ago, it was Thursday.
In three days, it will be Wednesday.

expressions.phrase: If today is Sunday, three days from now it will be Wednesday.
expressions.meaning_ar: إذا كان اليوم الأحد، فبعد ثلاثة أيام من الآن سيكون الأربعاء.
expressions.meaning_en: Counting forward three days from Sunday.
expressions.example: If today is Sunday, three days from now it will be Wednesday.

expressions.phrase: If today is Saturday, three days ago it was Wednesday.
expressions.meaning_ar: إذا كان اليوم السبت، فقبل ثلاثة أيام كان الأربعاء.
expressions.meaning_en: Counting back three days from Saturday.
expressions.example: If today is Saturday, three days ago it was Wednesday.

expressions.meaning_en: On the same day last week...
expressions.example: A week ago, I was on holiday.

grammar.title: ago = past (with was / past tense)
grammar.explanation_ar: ago تأتي بعد المدة وتدل على الماضي محسوبًا من الآن، ونستعمل معها الماضي (was). لنعدّ الأيام نرجع إلى الخلف ولا نعدّ اليوم الحالي.
grammar.explanation_en: "Ago" comes after the time period and shows the past, counted from now. Use the past tense (was). Count backwards, and don't count today.
examples: If today is Saturday, three days ago it was Wednesday.
I bought this phone two months ago.

grammar.title: from now = future (with will be)
grammar.explanation_ar: from now تأتي بعد المدة وتدل على المستقبل، ونستعمل معها will be. نعدّ إلى الأمام بدون حساب اليوم الحالي.
grammar.explanation_en: "From now" comes after the time period and shows the future; use "will be". Count forward, without counting today.
examples: If today is Sunday, three days from now it will be Wednesday.
Two weeks from now, I will be in Cairo.

grammar.title: in + time = future
grammar.explanation_ar: صيغة أخرى للمستقبل: in + المدة في أول العبارة: In three days, it will be Tuesday.
grammar.explanation_en: Another future form: in + period, at the start: In three days, it will be Tuesday.
examples: If today is Saturday, in three days it will be Tuesday.
In two months, I will finish the course.

grammar.title: Say "a week ago", not "seven days ago"
grammar.explanation_ar: للحديث عن اليوم نفسه من الأسبوع الماضي نقول a week ago. ويمكن استعمال الصيغ نفسها مع الأشهر: three months ago, two months from now.
grammar.explanation_en: For the same day last week, say "a week ago". The same patterns work with months: three months ago, two months from now.
examples: A week ago, it was Saturday too.
Three months from now, it will be summer.
